_doc: THE SECOND AXIS — what a place IS socially, beside `cat`, which is what it SELLS.
Nan 2026-09-06: 'Mot Dang admits a place by its counter — this is flat wrong.'
`cat` is a shopping axis and is good at its job; nothing here replaces it and no
canonical record is rewritten. `kind` is derived at build time by kind_layer.py
from the rules below, and an explicit top-level `kind` on a curated record wins.
The point of the axis is `answers`: what counts as this record ANSWERING A
QUESTION depends on the kind of place it is. A phone number is the answer a shop
owes. A wat owes its sect and its founding; a library owes what it holds and who
may read there. Judging every place by a shop's answer is the counter rule, and
the counter rule is what this file exists to end.
Rules are read in order and ACCUMULATE — a place can be more than one kind. A
record no rule claims comes back `unclassified`; that is a review item, never a
coin flip, and tests/test_kinds.py prints the count.

_doc: What it means for a record of this kind to ANSWER A QUESTION — the second gate.
`fields` are top-level record fields, `attrs` are keys under attrs, `ants` are
the nine-ant keys build.py already computes. A record answers if ANY listed
item is present. `future` names fields that do not exist yet (they arrive with
the field work); they are listed so the slot is ready and so nothing has to be

parking._why: THE PIN IS THE ANSWER, and this is the only kind where that is true. Every other kind can be pinned and still say nothing — a noodle stall with a coordinate and no phone, no hours and no menu has not answered anybody. The question asked of a car park IS 'where is there one near here', so a lot with an exact pin and nothing else has answered it in full. Nan, 2026-09-06: 'Of course we want unnamed lots to publish!' The fee, the access and the capacity are the second question, and 792 of the 1,796 already carry at least one of them.
parking._why_no_capacity_motorcycle: capacity:motorcycle is imported but not listed here: OSM carries it 0 times in TH-50 and TH-57 today, and an answer-set may only name evidence we hold.

_ants_doc: THE NINE ANTS, RE-CUT. build.py's completeness swarm was nine fixed slots and
four of them were a way to contact a seller — so a wat, a reading room or a
cemetery could never score above 2 of 9 however well we knew it, and ant_rank
feeds both the ranking and held(). That is the counter rule at the ranking
layer, and this is where it ends.
Nine stays nine — it is ก้าว, and a full swarm is a complete listing. Five
slots are universal (Thai name, English name, photo, owner-confirmed,
recently-walked); four are the kind's own. `commerce` keeps phone/LINE/hours/
website exactly as before, so nothing on the shopping axis moves by a pixel.
Each slot: [key, th, en]. `key` is a top-level record field, an attrs key, or
one of the ant keys build.py computes itself (phone·line·hours·web resolve
through channels(), which knows a dead website from a live one). An `attrs.`
prefix reads under attrs. A `|` lets one slot be answered by either of two
keys where the corpus records the same fact two ways.

_edge_doc: THE EDGE — decision J, Nan 2026-09-06: 'bus shelters, tree shrines, named sois,
wells — love all of these.' They are IN. Four classes that share one property
neither commerce nor an institution has: NOBODY WILL EVER CLAIM THEM. No owner
fills in a bus shelter's opening hours; there is no proprietor of a tree. So the
whole enrichment model the directory was built on — owner-confirmed, a phone to
ring, a listing to claim — is void here, and the only sources are the map, the
survey (somebody walked past and wrote it down), the municipal asset register,
and what the neighbourhood knows. Call that posture THE COMMONS.
Two further properties follow from it. They are NOT DISCRETE the way a shop is:
a soi is a line, a well serves a neighbourhood, a shrine may be one of a cluster.
And they are the fabric a reader navigates BY rather than TO — nobody searches
for a bus shelter by name; a shelter is the answer inside another answer. That
makes bearings (WO-64) matter more to this class than pins do.
They are also the most fragile thing in the catalogue. A shop that closes is
re-mapped by the next crawler. A yang-na avenue felled for a road widening, a
well capped, a หอเสื้อบ้าน cleared for a car park — nobody re-finds those.
KNOWN LIMITATION, written down rather than hidden: `claimed` (owner-confirmed)
is one of the five universal ants and a commons record can almost never earn it,
so these kinds realistically cap at 8 of 9. It is left universal because moving
it would reorder the strip on every shop page, and the shopping axis has not
been moved. The honest fix, when Nan wants it, is a `vouched`
path: a keeper recorded — the wat that tends the shrine, the tambon that keeps
the well, the family on the donor plaque — earning the same ant.
